title: The excursion band and how the Chicago jobs were arranged
summary: Howard names the men he took north and explains that a railroad porter hired the band and arranged the Chicago dances.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You had your full band, six pieces or so, was it good, huh? I see.
I know I had eight.
Eight, big band. Eight pieces, yeah.
The whole band went up there. Yeah, because I had taken Guy Kelly, which was a wonderful band, and I had taken a band, which was a wonderful trumpet man, you heard of him.
You made a couple records.
Well I'm the one taking him to Chicago.
Was that right man?

His people were there, his mother I think, and I dead hit him, you understand, and put a few dollars on him, which he played, you understand, and Poissy, uh, uh. Percy Umphrey. Percy Umphrey. Yeah, Percy Umphrey. He went with me, old man Joe Howard, Eddie Jones with Wicked Widow.
Howard played second trumpet then, not the trumpet. No, no, he played the tuba.
Tuba? Yeah, he played the tuba. He played the tuba, Henry Harden, which he's dead now, he's gone, and Henry. Yeah.
Then you played, you'd have those special dances at the Royal Rick, or did the organization put the, who hired you to go out? Did some be some lodge, or the railroad? No, no, it wasn't no lodge.
It was a guy by the name of Andrew, Andrew Jackson, I think that was the man. Anyway, he waited for the railroad. And the railroad. He put it on a hot, I would be dead. I know that he was head of it.
I have heard of excursions like say the Elks or something would hire a band when they go to a contention. Yeah, but no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no. Nothing like that.
The railroad. This guy waited for the people, he was a porter or something on the train, and he made connections some kind of way, and that's the way it would come out. He would hire the band.
Yeah. And when you got to Chicago, how did you get these jobs at the Royal Rick, or how was that arranged?
Well, that was arranged by him.
He had that whole thing. Yeah, he had all that, all that street. One big deal.
Yeah, see, well he knew all that, but I think he was working out from that, some kind of way he knew how to make the connection.
That'd be just open to the public, anybody go in there and see?
Anybody be at the door. And I mean the people from here, the people come leave from here on the excursion, well.
When you'd be there four or five days, how many nights did you work up there?
I work up maybe about two nights, that's all. About two nights, that's all.
